BT21 is genius, of course, but the BTS tour merch or the official merch Bighit offers is often really...basic and uninspired IMO. I love collecting merch for example but I've never really felt the need to get anything of that cause it all looks so bland it doesn't feel interesting enough for me to get. western fans do it too. Taylor was encouraging people with her last album, the more you bought the more you got a shot at getting especially good tour tickets or something. Harry Styles had a whole bunch of versions available. No photobook, but also clearly appealing to collector fans. Demi Lovato's fans posted themselves buying 5 copies of her album. BSB and Nsync fans were also competing back in the day, ppl bought multiple copies. Britney vs Christina had ppl do it as well. As soon as something is a competition and there is a sizable hardcore fandom, bulk buying just happens.

I agree with this tbh. Somi was always the most hyped (internationally) in IOI and she built her name up after as well with all those solo activities. Wanna One was always Kang Daniel and friends to a point. Wonyoung isn't anywhere at that level in IZ*ONE, there are several members who are around the same level of popularity and Sakura is arguably more popular internationally.

I think BTS right now are in the unique position of being the only real moneymaker at a small private company that doesn't have to answer to outside forces in terms of stocks etc. So they have quite a lot of freedom and leeway. I also think some people at Bighit at the very least have good intentions and take making music seriously as well as giving the boys some artistic freedom.

However, I am reluctant to consider them the ideal K-Pop company or say they're always right. On the flipside of solo stans blaming the company for every single thing, you've got quite a lot of fans who get mad about every single criticism of them. BH is a nice enough company overall, that doesn't mean they're perfect or "always know best". They've made quite a few mistakes in the time BTS has been in the spotlight, more when BTS was less popular than they are now. For example there's the misconception that the members make the final decision what their songs really will sound like, when it's very clear from a few statements that it's the company. I wasn't a BTS fan in 2015, just a general K-Pop fan (casual) and to me Bighit looked like any other company, working the guys to the bone to cash in on their upwards trajectory, mediaplaying their successes to increase their standing, etc. Even artistically, they've made choices that were baffling (the Berlin photoshoot, TxT's new fandom name). And while I don't think the boys had a problem with the crying scenes in the new DVD for example, if I think of Taehyung on Malta, he definitely didn't seem to want to be filmed, he walked away, as far from the cameras as possible, they still followed him. I don't think we should attack BH for every thing, but I also think it's dangerous to think of them as a benevolent, friendly entity that is above criticism.
